title.ko: 격식 있는 이메일과 일상 이메일 비교
title.en: formal vs informal emails: register and polite requests

explain.ko: 이메일은 읽는 사람과의 관계에 따라 격식을 달리합니다. 격식 있는 글(회사·학교·낯선 사람)은 Dear Sir or Madam / Dear Mr Lee로 시작하고, I am writing to ...로 목적을 밝히며, I would be grateful if you could ...처럼 정중한 요청을 하고, Best regards / Yours faithfully로 끝냅니다. 줄임말(I'm, don't)을 쓰지 않고 완전한 문장으로 씁니다. 일상적인 글(친구·가족)은 Hi로 시작하고, Could you ...? / Can you ...?로 부탁하며, See you soon / Write soon으로 끝낼 수 있습니다.
explain.en: The level of formality in an email depends on your relationship with the reader. A formal email (to a company, school or stranger) opens with Dear Sir or Madam / Dear Mr Lee, states the purpose with I am writing to ..., makes polite requests such as I would be grateful if you could ... and ends with Best regards / Yours faithfully. Avoid contractions (I'm, don't) and use full sentences. An informal email (to a friend or family member) opens with Hi, asks with Could you ...? / Can you ...? and can end with See you soon / Write soon.

questions.q: How does the man suggest ending a formal email?

lines.t: The tone of an email depends on who you are writing to. When you write to a company or school, start with Dear Sir or Madam, write formally and end with Best regards. With a friend you can start with Hi, write casually and end with See you soon.

trans.ko: 이메일은 읽는 사람에 따라 말투가 다릅니다. 회사나 학교에 쓸 때는 Dear Sir or Madam으로 시작해 격식 있게 쓰고 Best regards로 끝냅니다. 친구에게는 Hi로 시작해 편하게 쓰고 See you soon으로 끝낼 수 있습니다.

task.model: Dear Sir or Madam, I am writing to enquire about your English course. I would be grateful if you could tell me the schedule and the fee. I attach my CV. I look forward to your reply.

model_trans.en: Dear Sir or Madam, I am writing to enquire about your English course. I would be grateful if you could tell me the schedule and the fee. I attach my CV. I look forward to your reply.
